segments.narration: In 1892, a New England night sky turned blood red. Panic swept through towns as church bells rang out across the frozen countryside. People rushed outdoors in their nightclothes, staring upward at the eerie crimson canopy.

Streetlights flickered and died. Telegraph wires across the globe began sparking and sending messages on their own without batteries. Operators watched in sheer disbelief as equipment caught fire from invisible currents surging through the lines.
What was actually ripping through the atmosphere? Astronomers pointed their brass telescopes at a colossal sunspot erupting across the sun's surface.
A massive coronal mass ejection from that giant sunspot slammed straight into Earth's magnetic field, supercharging the upper air.

The terrifying glow wasn't an omen at all. It was simply nitrogen and oxygen colliding with intense solar radiation in the upper atmosphere, creating the most powerful auroral storm in modern history.
